title: Variant Sifter documentation
bodyHtml:
The Variant Sifter is an in-development module that allows you to explore, filter, and prioritize genetically associated variants, credible sets, and tissue-specific epigenomic annotations across a region, providing decision support for prioritization of variants and genes for further research.

All genomic coordinates are in the hg19 (GRCh37) genome build.

The current Variant Sifter is in beta testing mode and exists in two analogous interfaces: one that queries multi-ancestry genetic associations and another that queries single-ancestry genetic associations (when available for the chosen region). Both versions access the same credible sets and genomic and epigenomic annotations.

NOTE: the Variant Sifter is updated frequently. If you have not used it for some time, you may need to clear your browser cache before using it.

The Variant Sifter is part of the Knowledge Portal Integrative analysis workflow.

Quick start guide:

  • Start by choosing a phenotype. Start typing a keyword in the Phenotype field, then select a phenotype from the drop-down list.
  • Then set a genomic region: either enter a region in the format 'chromosome_number:start_coordinate-end_coordinate' (e.g., 8:117912512-118238953) or enter a gene name to set the region to the coordinates of that gene. If you enter a gene name, the region retrieved will be the coding sequence of the gene plus 100 kb of upstream and downstream flanking sequences.
  • The table of variants at the bottom displays all variants in the region that are associated with the chosen phenotype with p-value ≤ 0.05.
  • To change or add phenotypes, choose another phenotype in the Phenotype field as above, and then make a selection from the "Compare data" menu:
    • 'New search' removes the data on the page and initiates a new search.
    • 'Only overlapping' displays association plots for each phenotype and a "Combined" plot showing variants that are significantly associated with all added phenotypes. Only the shared variants are added to the table below.
    • 'All' displays association plots for each phenotype and a plot with all variants that are associated with all added phenotypes. All variants are added to the table below.
  • To mark individual variants with a star, click a star icon in the table, or click the star icon in the information popup for a specific variant on the region plot.
  • To filter the variants by credible set membership, click the "Select Credible Sets" menu and select one or more credible sets. The variant table then displays only the credible set variants.
  • To filter the variants by their overlap with tissue-specific epigenomic annotations, click the "Select Annotation" menu in the "Filter associated variants by location within regulatory regions annotated in broad tissue categories" section. To guide your selection of annotation types and tissues, the Global Enrichment plot on the right shows you which tissue-specific annotations are enriched genome-wide for genetic associations with the selected phenotype, as determined by stratified LD score regression. Select an annotation type, then select one or more tissues. The variant table is filtered to display only those variants located within annotations of the selected type in the selected tissue. You may make multiple selections of annotation types and tissues. Above the table, you can select "And" or "Or" in the "Compare annotated regions" menu to see the intersection or the union of variants located within multiple annotation types.
  • To see annotations in specific cell or tissue types within each tissue category: in the visualization of annotation patterns in broad tissue groups, click on one or more tracks of interest. This displays a new visualization below, showing annotations in the specific cell/tissue types within that group. Mouse over an annotation to see more details. Click specific tracks to filter the table to show only those cell/tissue types.
  • To filter the variants by their overlap with regions linked to genes, click "Filter associated variants by links to genes". 
  • To see all supporting evidence and link to the original supporting datasets at the Common Metabolic Diseases Genome Atlas, click the "View" button in the table.
